text:
maria: Heads-up — CI perf regression alarm for eu-west-1 L4 cluster right after merge #5129. p99 token latency +28% on A10 hosts, throughput dip on long prompts. Blocking rollout. @kevin @sanjay
kevin: saw the alert. which corridors (KV/cache/kernel) are suspicious? any related e2e failures?
sanjay: quick check: CI logs show increased CPU sys time and spikes on kernel-selector path around kernel_pick_v2() after merge. No memory OOMs.
ci-bot: [CI] perf-check pipeline failed: perf-regress-eu-w1 (p99: 163ms -> 209ms). Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/compare/5128..5129
maria: attaching a short perf snippet from a repro run on a dev L4 node:
```
# top stacks (sampled, 10s)
25% kernel_selector::pick_best
18% scheduler::batch_window
12% kvcache::evict_and_refill
8% net::rx_poll_irq
5% aten::matmul_kernel
```
```
# `ethtool -S` shows rx_packets and rx_interrupts spiking on eth0
rx_packets: 2.1M -> 3.8M
rx_interrupts: 8k -> 35k
```
kevin: net IRQ spike + kernel selector churn — interesting. Could be small-packet flooding from a noisy neighbor causing scheduler to fall back to less efficient kernels. Any NIC metrics from host-level exporter?
ops-bot: host-metrics: eu-w1-l4-03 -> NIC rx_q_len high, irq_affinity uneven. CPU steal is low. Link: https://infra.redwood/hosts/eu-w1-l4-03
alex: fwiw, PR 5129 changed kernel fallback priority: preferred vectorized kernel even for short sequence lengths when KV cache miss-rate > 30%. That could force heavier kernels on short seqs and amplify NIC processing cost if KV thrash increases requests per session.
sanjay: I ran a bisect locally between 5128 and 5129 -> add a tiny repro harness:
```
# reproduce
python tools/repro_long_prompts.py --model rwd-a10-l4 --seq 1024 --concurrency 8 --kv-seq 64
```
Results: 5128 p99=158ms, 5129 p99=208ms (consistent).
maria: logs show repeated kvcache eviction cycles at ~600ms intervals, correlating with kernel selector re-eval -> batch windows shrink -> CPU sys increase.
kevin: So chain is: noisy neighbor or ingress burst -> rx IRQs spike -> packets delivered interleaved -> kvcache misses increase -> kernel selector flips to heavy kernel -> latency spiral. Does that fit?
alex: yes. Also noticed kernel_picker now disables automatic batch-coalescing under certain miss patterns (accidental side-effect of the change). That reduces batching efficiency.
ci-bot: FR: kernel-picker change introduced in commit 9f3d2a (PR 5129).
maria: Recommendation: hold the rollout, revert PR 5129 in canary eu-west, optional hotfix: force previous kernel ordering + re-enable batch-coalescing.
kevin: Agreed — mark rollout halt. Can someone post the revert PR? I'll trigger a canary rollback.
sanjay: I'll open PR 5131 to revert 9f3d2a, include regression test that simulates KV miss patterns + short sequences.
kevin: Also ask infra to pin IRQ affinity on L4 A10 fleet in eu-west until we get root cause. ops-bot, can you schedule?
ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1283 to pin irqbalance profile and throttle small-packet flows on eu-w1 A10 pool. ETA 30m.
alex: For follow-up: we need a longer-term fix in kernel-selector: 1) add hardware-aware heuristics (prefer lightweight kernels on A10/L4 when rx_irq_high) 2) restore batch-coalescing guard 3) add synthetic CI test for kv thrash workload. I'll draft design doc.
maria: file issues: RUNTIME-432 (revert + test), RUNTIME-433 (kernel-selector heuristics), RUNTIME-434 (observability: per-host irq vs batching graph).
kevin: thanks team. action items: rollback in canary (me), revert PR (sanjay), infra pin IRQs (ops), design doc (alex). Keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
